answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks from trusted seeds, so a Sybil cluster cannot gain influence merely by adding internal edges. If its external boundary is sparse, its conductance—the cut size divided by the smaller side’s volume—is low, limiting walk flow across the cut and, under the protocol’s seed and mixing assumptions, bounding aggregate voting weight. A canyon-like boundary can isolate an onyx core from the nebula of honest attestations.
